text: A preparation of ATPase from the membranes of Micrococcus lysodeikticus, solubilized and more than 95% pure, showed two main bands in analytical polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis. They did not correspond to isoenzymes because one band could be converted into the other by exposure to a mildly acidic pH value. The conversion was paralleled by changes in molecular weight, circular dichroism, and catalytic properties. Denaturation by pH at 25 degrees C was followed by means of circular dichroism, ultracentrifugation, and polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis. A large conformational transition took place in the basic range with midpoints at about pH = 9.6 (I = 10(-4) M), 10.3 (I = 0.03 M), and 11.3 (I = 0.1 M). The transition was reversible. Weak aggregation of the protein occurred in this range of pH. The final product was largely random coil, but even at pH 1.5 dissociation into individual subunits was not complete. However, partial dissociation took place at pH 5 (I = 0.028 M). At this pH value the enzyme was active, but 20-30% of the activity could be recovered when the pH was returned to 7.5. In the acidic region the midpoint of the transition occurred near pH = 4.6 (I = 0.028 M). The pK of most of the tyrosine residues of the protein was about 10.9. The unfolding was reversible and the protein was soon converted into peptide species with molecular weights higher than those determined for the subunits by gel electrophoresis in the presence of sodium dodecyl sulfate. Conventional proteolysis accounted for the transformation.
